# IMON.world

> Sabbir Hassan Imon's personal site: software projects, a pixel-art world, browser games, and free browser-based learning labs. Static site, no server-side runtime, optional aggregate usage counts, no accounts required for learning.

This file is a plain-text map of the site for language models and other automated readers. Every URL below is a real page. Nothing here is a marketing claim beyond what the pages themselves state.

## Site facts

- Canonical domain: https://imon.com.bd/
- Owner: Sabbir Hassan Imon (also known as IMON, GitHub handle `sabbirimon`)
- Built from South Asia
- Published on GitHub Pages as a folder of plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript files. There is no build step, no bundler, no server-side runtime.
- Optional aggregate usage counts are consent-based. Approximate IP location for weather and the atlas is a separate choice.
- Third-party APIs are contacted from the browser only; see https://imon.com.bd/privacy.html for the complete list and exactly what each one receives.
- All game currency is fictional. No real money, payments, wagers or cash value anywhere on the site.
- The owner maintains this site with AI-assisted development. Source code is public.

## Pages

- [Human-readable site map](https://imon.com.bd/sitemap.html)
- [Mystery quest journal](https://imon.com.bd/quests.html) — six trails with 24 clues and challenges.

### [Course catalog](https://imon.com.bd/courses.html)
All exercises are linked in static HTML, arranged by course and chapter. The [JSON course index](https://imon.com.bd/data/course-index.json) supplies each exercise ID, title, brief and absolute workbench URL. Each course also has a five-question quiz with explanations, accessible at its quizUrl. Reading the catalog and practicing require no account. The Python practice studio adapts 96 Exercism cases, and the HTML table workshop adapts MDN examples. Both run locally and offer worked answers. Private results are at https://imon.com.bd/progress.html and opt-in practice totals appear on the [practice leaderboard](https://imon.com.bd/leaderboard.html).


The [learning library](https://imon.com.bd/library.html) contains additional courses, labs and articles published by the site editor.

### [Systems Lab](https://imon.com.bd/systems.html)
Fourteen browser-only simulations cover IPv4 subnets, VLANs, device troubleshooting, queues, caching, cloud compute and retention, update rollout, recovery points, binary signals, sampling, model recall and resistor dividers. Each has an interactive model, prediction, worked method and local check. The four labs award levels for distinct solved exercises and a badge for finishing each chapter.

### [Home](https://imon.com.bd/)
The main site. Sections:
- [Projects](https://imon.com.bd/#projects) — software from Sabbir Hassan Imon, including OmniCast and OmniRecovery.
- [HyperL](https://imon.com.bd/hyperl/) — Experimental AI compute with sharding, memory-tier planning, SafeTensors tools and authenticated workers.
- [Meshlit](https://imon.com.bd/meshlit/) — local GGUF chat and agents on Android, plus a native desktop coding workspace and device pairing.
- [Pixel world](https://imon.com.bd/#pixel-world) — an illustrated pixel scene with a live weather layer, World Studio controls, day/night cycle and optional synthesised ambience.
- [Arcade](https://imon.com.bd/#arcade) — free browser games: Snake, Surf, 2048, Ludo, Puzzle, Dev Slots and a racer. No payments, no wagers.
- [Daily](https://imon.com.bd/#news) — live technology and science/space headlines plus a daily computer-science quiz.
- [Map](https://imon.com.bd/#map) — a searchable atlas with 176 country and territory outlines and optional approximate country selection.
- [Achievements](https://imon.com.bd/#achievements) — badges earned from the games and labs.
- [About](https://imon.com.bd/#about) — who the owner is, toolkit and current focus.

### [Code Lab](https://imon.com.bd/lab.html)
A browser practice lab for HTML, CSS and JavaScript. A lesson panel on the left; a workbench on the right with a file rail, editor, live preview and terminal. Exercises come from an imported curriculum (`html-101`, `css-101`) plus a built-in taster course. Every exercise has a goal, study material, exam instructions and an outcome. A correct answer pays XP and animates a coin burst. A wrong answer explains what is wrong, which file and line it is in, and how to fix it. Each note card can search Stack Overflow for real questions about the tag or property it covers.

### [AI Lab](https://imon.com.bd/ai-lab.html)
Learn Python, machine learning and system design through 66 exercises in six chapters: Python for models, AI safety, System design, Working with APIs, Working with data, Python practice studio. The Python runs in the browser through a small teaching interpreter — a tokenizer, parser and executor, not a full runtime. It supports `def`/`return`, `if`/`elif`/`else`, `for`, `while`, lists, dictionaries, tuples, strings, common builtins and `import math`. Two browser-side learning modules extend it: a fake HTTP client for `api.example.com` (reached via `import requests` or `import http`) and an in-memory SQL engine (reached via `import sqlite3`). No account and no server are needed. The course data lives in `docs/data/ai-course.json`, so a new exercise is a JSON entry plus a reference answer.

### [Circuits & Signals](https://imon.com.bd/circuits.html)
Learn electronics and signals through 39 exercises in twelve chapters: voltage, current and resistance; Kirchhoff's laws; the voltage divider; capacitors and the RC circuit; inductors and the RL circuit; RLC, resonance and filters; diodes and rectification; LEDs and light; digital logic and gates; combinational design; sequential logic; and signals in the real world. The workbench has a parts bin, a board you place and wire parts on, and an oscilloscope that plots the probed node over time. The simulation engine is plain JavaScript with no dependencies: modified nodal analysis solves the resistive network, and capacitors and inductors use the trapezoidal companion model so a transient tracks the real exponential to within a fraction of a percent. Three kinds of exercise: a number checked with a tolerance, a written answer checked for the ideas it asks about, and a circuit checked against the topology it expects. A panel of further tools points at free open-source EDA that runs in the browser — EEcircuit, OpenCircuits, DigitalJS, aeCAD, Fluxa, OpenBench and EDAViewer. The course data lives in `docs/data/circuits-course.json` and the study material in `docs/circuits-chapters.js`.

### [Gridworks](https://imon.com.bd/gridworks/)
A standalone 18-city infrastructure management game with a pure simulation engine and a canvas UI. Power and data travel through separate layers; Cat6 reach, fibre capacity, generation, hardware, coverage, maintenance, prices and customer satisfaction determine service revenue. Later chapters unlock regional links, LEO ground stations and paid automation with budget reserves. Keyboard construction, touch pan/zoom, map overlays, fullscreen, pause/speed controls, and sound off by default. Saves live in the visitor's browser.

### [Developer Toolbox](https://imon.com.bd/tools/)
Offline-first developer utilities: JSON formatter and validator, YAML, Terraform, SQL and XML formatters, Base64 encoder/decoder, JWT decoder, timestamp converter, regex tester, UUID generator, hash generator, colour contrast checker, a DNS lookup tool, URL inspection, Unicode text counts, and a playable [sound library](https://imon.com.bd/tools/#sounds).

### [Privacy & data notice](https://imon.com.bd/privacy.html)
A hand-written notice listing every third-party service the browser contacts, every key written to local storage, what reaches the optional Supabase table when a visitor signs in, and what is never stored anywhere. It names MDN's search API as the first choice for the Code Lab lookup and explains that it was replaced because it sends no CORS header, so a static host cannot call it.

### [Log in](https://imon.com.bd/login.html)
Optional Google account registration and sign-in for private cloud progress. Signed-in players can also set an account password. Nothing is written for visitors who never sign in.

## Machine-readable companion

- [`/.well-known/agents.json`](https://imon.com.bd/.well-known/agents.json) — a machine-readable description of this site for AI agents: what it is, what it is not, the public entry points, the third-party services contacted, the licensing and privacy posture, and the machine-readable data files.
- [`/sitemap.xml`](https://imon.com.bd/sitemap.xml) — the canonical URL list.
- [`/robots.txt`](https://imon.com.bd/robots.txt) — crawling is allowed.

## Conventions for automated readers

- Prefer the canonical URLs above. The site also serves a GitHub Pages fallback path, but `https://imon.com.bd/` is canonical and should be used for links and citations.
- Query strings such as `?scene=waterfall-valley` select a pixel scene and are not separate pages; section fragments such as `#news` are not separate pages either.
- All pages are static HTML. There is no API to call for page content; read the HTML directly.
- Interactive features (the labs, games, map, weather) need a browser. There is no server-side rendering to scrape.
- A service worker caches the site's own files for offline use. It does not track, store or transmit anything about a visitor.
